recent_posts.title: Testing Methods: Non-text Contrast
recent_posts.summary: WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast requires UI components and informative graphics to maintain at least a 3:1 contrast ratio against adjacent colors. The guide explores three testing approaches: automated tools excel at quickly identifying common contrast issues but struggle with complex visuals and context; AI-powered testing can process large amounts of visual content but may miss purpose and context; manual testing provides real-world usability evaluation and catches nuanced issues but can be time-consuming and subjective. The most effective strategy combines all three methods, starting with automated tools for broad coverage and following up with manual testing for thorough evaluation.

recent_posts.title: ARIA and Real World Dangers
recent_posts.summary: ARIA should be used as a precise surgical tool to fill HTML's semantic gaps, not as a blanket solution. Common mistakes include overusing aria-label on non-interactive elements and creating mismatches between visible text and screen reader announcements. HTML should always be the first choice, with ARIA applied only when necessary and with deep understanding to avoid breaking accessibility.

recent_posts.title: Baby Steps Accessibility
recent_posts.summary: Organizations often underestimate the scope and complexity of making PDFs accessible at scale. Key accessibility requirements include proper tagging, descriptive titles, and language declarations. While tools like PDF Accessibility Checker (PAC) help with individual files, enterprise-level initiatives require strategic planning, vendor partnerships, and prioritization of active content over archived materials. Remediation costs depend on page count and content complexity, with dynamically generated PDFs requiring template-level fixes. Success demands ongoing training to prevent future accessibility debt and embed best practices into content creation workflows.

recent_posts.title: Testing Methods: Reflow
recent_posts.summary: WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow requires content to display without horizontal scrolling at 320px width or 400% zoom, benefiting users with low vision and mobile users. Testing approaches include automated tools for quick detection of layout issues, AI for efficient cross-viewport analysis, and manual testing for nuanced validation. Each method has limitations, making a combined approach most effective for ensuring compliance and real-world usability.

recent_posts.title: Digital Accessibility is a Journey, Not a Destination
recent_posts.summary: Digital accessibility requires ongoing commitment rather than one-time implementation. Technology changes, team turnover, evolving user needs, and updated standards mean accessibility work is never complete. Organizations should integrate accessibility into daily workflows, provide continuous training, test with disabled users, and measure progress over time to create truly inclusive digital products.

recent_posts.title: Testing Methods: Images of Text (No Exception)
recent_posts.summary: WCAG 1.4.9 Images of Text (No Exception) is a Level AAA accessibility criterion requiring real text instead of images of text, with exceptions only for essential visual presentations or branding. The guideline benefits users with low vision, visual tracking difficulties, and cognitive disabilities. Testing approaches include automated tools for quick detection, AI-based methods for intelligent analysis, and manual testing for contextual judgment. A combined approach using all three methods provides the most comprehensive and effective testing strategy.

recent_posts.title: Baby Steps Accessibility
recent_posts.summary: Page titles serve as crucial navigation aids for screen reader users and accessibility. Common issues include missing titles, vague descriptions, identical titles across pages, poor information ordering, and mismatches with page content. Best practices include making titles present, unique, descriptive, properly ordered with specific content first, and consistent with main headings.

recent_posts.title: Testing Methods: Visual Presentation
recent_posts.summary: WCAG 1.4.8 Visual Presentation is a Level AAA success criterion that ensures users can customize text appearance for better readability. It requires user-selectable colors, text blocks under 80 characters wide, no justified text, proper line spacing, and 200% text resizing capability. The criterion primarily benefits people with cognitive disabilities. Testing approaches include automated tools for detecting justified text and character limits, AI for analyzing visual patterns, and manual testing for real-world usability. A combined approach using all three methods provides the most comprehensive assessment of compliance and usability.

recent_posts.title: Baby Steps Accessibility
recent_posts.summary: Color contrast issues affect 79.1% of websites according to WebAIM's analysis. This guide covers how to identify and fix text contrast problems using browser developer tools, accessibility extensions like ARC Toolkit and axe DevTools, and manual eyedropper tools. Regular text needs a 4.5:1 contrast ratio while large text requires 3:1. The post provides practical testing methods for different scenarios including text over images and PDFs.

recent_posts.title: Introducing Baby Steps Accessibility
recent_posts.summary: A new article series called 'Baby Steps Accessibility' launches to help beginners improve digital product accessibility through simple, actionable tasks. The series targets those new to accessibility who don't know where to start, emphasizing that small improvements can be made without waiting for executive support, funding, or vendor assistance. The approach focuses on grassroots efforts and low-hanging fruit improvements that can be implemented immediately.
